BILL NUMBER:  S1948              REVISED 04/15/09

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act in relation to authorizing and directing the department of
labor to study workplace abuse and harassment


 PURPOSE :
Directs the Department of Labor (DOL) to study workplace abuse and
harassment and to report to the Legislature and the Governor, within
one year, its findings and recommendations for reducing such abuse and
harassment.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Section 1 sets forth legislative findings.

Section 2 directs DOL to study hostile workplace behaviors and their
costs, and to make recommendations to the Legislature and Governor
within 1 year of the effective date of the act.

 JUSTIFICATION :
Studies have documented that abusive work environments can have
serious adverse effects on targeted employees, including feelings of
shame and humiliation, stress, loss of sleep, anxiety, depression,
stress related gastrointestinal disorders and hypertension. They also
suggest that abusive work environments can also harm employers, by
resulting in lower employee productivity and morale, higher turnover
and absenteeism, and greater medical and workers' compensation claims.
This legislation directs the Department of Labor to undertake a study
on abusive work environments, and to make recommendations about
addressing such behavior.

2007-2008:  A.4921 Advanced to 3rd Reading/S.2715 Referred to Rules
2006:       S.8018 Referred to Rules/A.11565 Referred to Labor

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
Undetermined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately upon enactment.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2006: S.8018/A.11565 No action.
